exposure: delivery doctor type (hospital staff obstetrician vs. locum doctor)
cohort: The study included 1,323 deliveries in 2017 and 1,463 deliveries in 2019 from a type 2 maternity ward, excluding medical terminations of pregnancy and births before 22 weeks of gestation.
finding: The presence of locum obstetricians did not significantly impact the overall rate of Caesarean sections, severe maternal, or severe perinatal morbidities, but was associated with a significant increase in forceps-assisted deliveries.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the overall rate of Caesarean sections between the two periods, but a significant increase in forceps-assisted deliveries was noted when locum doctors were present.
